teams.heading: Six Nations and Sanzaar bid to scrap 2030 relegation with Fiji bottom
teams.body: The fight over the Nations Championship's relegation mechanism remains unsettled. Last week the Guardian reported that the Six Nations and Sanzaar face a fresh battle with World Rugby in their bid to remove the drop from the competition, with the threat due to arrive in 2030. No agreement on that structure has yet been reported. Fiji go into this weekend's Round 6 trip to Italy in Udine 12th of 12, without a win in five and with a points difference of -161.

teams.heading: Asher Opoku-Fordjour pays tribute to single mum Rebecca on England podcast
teams.body: England and Sale Sharks prop Asher Opoku-Fordjour, 22, has told the England Rugby Podcast how his mum, Rebecca, raised him and his three brothers alone while working to provide for them. "We didn't realise how tough it was on her until you look back," he said. A footballer as a boy, he took up rugby only at 10, when his dad, having watched a Six Nations game, took him to the local rugby club. England, fresh from beating Japan 78-15, face New Zealand on Saturday.

lead.why: The only new England men's story since the last edition; the others are background or already reported.

teams.heading: Matthieu Jalibert takes fly-half role in Bleus training, set to face Argentina
teams.body: Rugbyrama reports one firm answer from Tuesday's first full session at Marcoussis: Jalibert will run the game against the Pumas at the Stade de France on Saturday. That gives France a more conventional half-back pairing after captain Antoine Dupont's improvised stint in the No. 10 jersey against South Africa. Outside back Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang was spared, his Pau teammate Grégoire Arfeuil stepping in, with the rest of the backline almost unchanged. France must win to be certain of a place in the Nations Championship final in London.

lead.why: Fresh selection news: Tuesday's training puts Jalibert back at fly-half for Saturday, which moves on Sunday's 'nears return' story.

teams.heading: Simon Easterby questions spirit of Rassie Erasmus' late Springbok front-row switches
teams.body: Ireland assistant coach Simon Easterby is wary of more last-minute Springbok selection changes before Saturday's Nations Championship test at the Aviva Stadium. Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus moved Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit from the bench into his starting front row shortly before kick-off against France. Erasmus has hinted he could do so again depending on the team Ireland pick. Easterby said: "I'm not saying it's not in the spirit of the game, but maybe it's not in the spirit of the game."

lead.why: Fresh Ireland coaching-staff reaction to the Springboks' late-switch tactic before Saturday's test.

teams.heading: Italy's Argentina defeat draws 314,483 viewers, up on South Africa test
teams.body: Last Saturday's 14-19 defeat to Argentina in Genoa drew 314,483 Italian viewers. Free-to-air TV8 carried the bulk with 208,967, while 89,931 more watched the Sky Sport Uno simulcast and 15,585 tuned in on Sky Sport Arena. That beat the 294,345 who watched the 7-66 loss to South Africa a week earlier, and dwarfed the 60,883 Sky audience for Wales' win over New Zealand. Saturday's Fiji test in Udine is again on TV8, Sky Sport Arena and NOWtv.

lead.why: Fresh Italy-specific figures not yet covered; the other Italy stories have already led recent editions.

teams.heading: Scotland lose captain Sione Tuipulotu and three others for Japan finale
teams.body: Sunday's 15-12 win over Australia cost Scotland three more: Toulon scrum-half Ben White (knee), Toshiba Brave Lupus No. 8 Jack Dempsey (foot) and Glasgow lock Scott Cummings (leg), while Tuipulotu had pulled out late with a knee injury. Edinburgh forwards Grant Gilchrist and Magnus Bradbury and Leicester Tigers lock Cam Henderson join head coach Gregor Townsend's squad for Saturday's game against Japan at Murrayfield. Scrum coach Pieter de Villiers called Tuipulotu a "fantastic captain" but praised Glasgow team-mate Rory Darge, who led the side against the Wallabies, for stepping up.

lead.why: Four first-choice players, including the captain, are ruled out of Saturday's Round 6 test, the day's only fresh Scotland event.

teams.heading: Two arrested after Hirwaun pub fight following Wales' win over All Blacks
teams.body: South Wales Police are appealing for witnesses after a disturbance at the Glancynon Inn in Hirwaun, near Aberdare, at around 8.30pm on Saturday. Earlier that day, head coach Steve Tandy's side had beaten New Zealand 35-28 in Cardiff for a first win over the All Blacks since 1953. A fight is understood to have broken out inside the pub. Two people were arrested on suspicion of affray and have since been released on bail. Investigations are ongoing, and police have asked anyone who was inside the pub at the time to come forward.

lead.why: It is the only new item; the others retell the All Blacks win already covered this week.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi praises Pumas' character in Genoa win despite 13-man finish
teams.body: Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi conceded that Italy dominated possession and territory in the first half of Saturday's 19-14 win in Genoa, but said these matches are about converting chances and scoring. Above all he singled out his players' character, noting the side stayed connected through a fraught final 20 minutes, when yellow cards for Joel Sclavi and Efraín Elías left them with 13. He described a team still under construction, whose cohesion grows the longer it spends together, and noted the squad now has two weeks together.

lead.why: It is Argentina's head coach reacting to the Italy win, an angle not yet run after the Bernasconi and Midi Olympique editions.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby questions Les Kiss's authority after Wallabies' 15-12 Murrayfield defeat
teams.body: Wallabies head coach Les Kiss is clearly useful as a specialist or assistant, a Planet Rugby column argues, but nothing in his post-match comments after Sunday's 15-12 Nations Championship loss to Scotland suggested the standing or authority to sell a vision to players or public. The piece also dismisses rugby league recruits as 'sugar-hits' — with Mark Nawaqanitawase returning to union and Angus Crichton set to follow his Sydney Roosters teammate — insisting Australia must develop forwards and a reliable first five-eighth.

lead.why: The only NEW item (#1) is about South Africa's kick-chase and World Rugby's laws, not Australia's squad, result or coach, so this column on Les Kiss is the strongest Australia story.

teams.heading: Japan will face Scotland without captain Sione Tuipulotu and three injured team-mates
teams.body: Glasgow centre Tuipulotu, a late withdrawal from Sunday's win over Australia with a knee problem, misses Saturday's Nations Championship group finale against the Brave Blossoms at Murrayfield. Toulon scrum-half Ben White (knee), Toshiba Brave Lupus No. 8 Jack Dempsey (foot) and Glasgow lock Scott Cummings (leg) were all hurt in that game. Rory Darge, who led Scotland on Sunday, keeps the captaincy; head coach Gregor Townsend has called up Grant Gilchrist, Magnus Bradbury and Cam Henderson, and uncapped Glasgow back Josh McKay could debut.

teams.heading: Sir Steve Hansen says Wales loss 'reminded' him of World Cup exits
teams.body: Former All Blacks head coach Sir Steve Hansen told the Rugby Unity podcast that last weekend's 35-28 defeat to Wales came down to mindset: preparing well but subconsciously assuming victory means "we wait for things to happen and there's no urgency" until desperation sets in. He said the loss "reminded" him of the 2007 World Cup quarter-final defeat by France at the same Cardiff ground and the 19-7 semi-final defeat by England in 2019. He also felt the number of changes made by head coach Dave Rennie was a factor.

lead.why: It is the only new item about the All Blacks, with a former head coach diagnosing the Cardiff defeat.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus handed six-Test ban, will miss Saturday's Dublin clash with Ireland
teams.body: World Rugby moved swiftly after Monday's press conference in which the Springbok head coach asked whether officials were match-fixing, its disciplinary panel ruling "that the threshold for serious misconduct had been met." Erasmus had claimed officials missed 17 knee-drop tackles by France in last Friday's 21-19 defeat in Paris. The suspension also covers finals weekend and bars him from match-day contact with players and from media duties. South Africa Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing to explain he never meant to allege any official acted with ulterior motives.

lead.why: World Rugby's six-match ban is a material new development: it rules the head coach out of Saturday's test in Dublin.
